messages:
Priya Patel: Thanks for the all-hands — starting a short follow-up thread for process Qs (release cadence, oncall, quality bars, SLAs). Drop brief Qs and we'll answer live in ~20m.

Alex Chen: Quick: are we still targeting weekly release trains for hosted? noticed a few slips.

Priya Patel: Weekly remains the target for hosted API. Some trains slipped due to infra migrations and emergency rollbacks; we'll publish an exception policy and clearer comms.

Samir Gupta: Canary & rollback specifics? do runtime PRs need full perf pre-merge?

Priya Patel: Default canary 30m. Rollback triggers: error-rate >0.5% above baseline or p95 latency +15% sustained for 5m. Runtime-impacting PRs require smoke perf checks before merge; full perf suite runs post-merge and blocks promotion if it flags regressions. Add "perf-test" label for special runs.

Marta López: Oncall: any move to 2-week rotations? many folks burning out.

Priya Patel: We'll pilot 2-week infra rotations next quarter; runtime stays 1-week for now. Coverage: runtime 1 primary + 1 secondary; infra 1 primary + 2 secondaries. Rota template and shadow plan will be posted.

Alex Chen: SLA tiers? hosted still 99.9? Dedicated higher options?

Priya Patel: Hosted public SLA stays 99.9. Dedicated can opt into 99.95 with reserved capacity and contract terms. We'll publish an SLA matrix and examples.

Priya Patel: Action items: I'll draft a one-pager with thresholds. Marta to draft hosted vs dedicated release differences. Alex to mock console canary/route health UI. Post PRs to #eng-docs and we'll iterate.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for train/2026-03-25 (build 2026.03.25-c1d7).
